messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dedicated-eu-1' GPU utilization 99%, request queue length 1,230, autoscaler attempted 3x and failed. Throttling incoming requests for non-reserved tenants. Ticket: INC-2027
Samir: Oncall here. seeing huge queue growth and multiple enterprise tenants reporting high latency. paging infra and runtime. @Lia can you check autoscaler logs?
Mae: I’m jumping in — pulling autoscaler controller logs, attaching errors.
Mae: ```
I0224 12:41:21 autoscaler.go:217] desired=64 current=64 max=64
E0224 12:41:21 autoscaler.go:245] scale-failed: reached pool.max_replicas
```
Lia: hitting pool.max_replicas (64) — policy cap. We tried to scale but quota cap prevents. Also several pods in that pool are spiking GPU mem to 100% (likely noisy neighbor).
Chris: Any tenant IDs with heavy allocation? can we identify noisy pods?
Mae: Top GPUs: tenant:enterprise-acme-prod (reserved=8) shows steady usage, but tenant:research-sandbox has 20 long-running jobs consuming 40% of nodes. Logs show many tiny, high-concurrency jobs from that tenant.
Samir: That's our noisy neighbor — research-sandbox not enterprise, but they’re on the same dedicated pool due to overprovisioning earlier. Need quick mitigation to free reserved capacity for enterprise customers.
Lia: Options: 1) Evict low-priority tenant pods from the pool (taint/evict), 2) Move enterprise tenants to emergency-reserve pool if available, 3) Increase pool.max_replicas (requires infra quota bump, slow).
Kyle: We need to inform affected customers ASAP. Support, can you blast a status update about degraded performance for some enterprise tenants? Mark it as partial degradation for dedicated customers in eu-west-1.
Support: On it — drafting notice. Will link once posted.
Mae: Trying a targeted eviction: `kubectl get pods -n tenant-research-sandbox -o wide --selector=pool=dedicated-eu-1` then `kubectl drain` on noisy nodes. Doing now.
Mae: ```
# evict low-priority jobs
kubectl delete pods -n research-sandbox --selector=job-type=interactive --grace-period=5
```
OpsBot: Eviction initiated on 6 pods. ETA for pod termination ~30s.
Samir: Good. After eviction, we should re-evaluate queue and allow reserved tenants to grow. Lia, do we have affinity rules to keep enterprise on reserved nodes?
Lia: yes, reserved nodes have label `reserved=true` and enterprise tenants are supposed to be pinned, but some enterprise workloads spilled due to earlier node failure. We can migrate back by updating routing policy.
Chris: I’m flipping routing for enterprise to emergency-reserve pool now. Will route by tenant-id for the next 20 minutes. Command in managed router: `route set --tenant enterprise-* --pool emergency-reserve-eu`
Chris: Done. 8 enterprise tenants switched.
Mae: Queue length dropping: 1,230 -> 420 -> 120 in last 3 mins. Throttling percent reduced to 8%.
Samir: Nice. Monitor for regression. We still need to address autoscaler cap — customers will keep growing. Lia, can we temporarily bump pool.max_replicas to 80? Is there a quick approval path?
Lia: Manual override exists but requires infra on-call to approve and increased cloud quota. I can open a support request for quota now — but that will take ~30–90m. For immediate relief, we should enforce per-tenant concurrency limits on non-enterprise to prevent re-occurrence.
Kyle: Agree — long-term we need rate limits. For now, throttle research-sandbox to 10 concurrent.
Mae: Applying per-tenant throttling rule: `redwoodctl policies create --tenant research-sandbox --concurrency 10 --priority low` — applied.
OpsBot: Throttle policy created and enforced.
Samir: Support update?
Support: Status update posted: "Partial degradation for dedicated-eu-1: increased latency and request throttling for some dedicated customers. Engineering investigating; mitigation in progress. Enterprises prioritized." Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2027
Kyle: Sales heads: I’ll loop in AE managers for impacted enterprise tenants for potential SLA credits.
Chris: Autoscaler logs show repeated failures due to pool-level max and cloud quota error: `insufficient-quota GPUs: requested 16, available 0`. We need to request quota increase from cloud provider. Opening ticket now.
Lia: Cloud ticket opened: CT-88932; ETA 3h for quota increase. We should not rely on that.
Mae: Proposing follow-ups: 1) enforce stricter tenant isolation (move noisy tenants to shared pool), 2) add autoscaler fallback to spin short-lived preemptible nodes (lower SLO but prevents throttling), 3) postmortem and rate-limit rollout.
Samir: Agreed. For now checklist: - keep enterprise routing to emergency-reserve for 2h - keep per-tenant throttle on research-sandbox - monitor queue and notify if >200 for >5m - Support to update affected customers with mitigation and ETA for full restore
Mae: I'll monitor dashboards and post periodic updates every 5m. Current metrics: GPU util 76% (after migration), queue 92, throttling 6%.
Samir: Handing off to Mae for next 30m. I’ll remain reachable. New oncall: Mae is primary; Samir fallback.
Mae: Acknowledged. Starting incident log. Adding action items in PagerDuty.
Support: Posted second update: "Mitigation in progress: noisy tenant evicted and throttled; enterprise traffic re-routed to reserved pool. Partial service restored. Engineers continuing remediation."
OpsBot: Reminder scheduled: Incident follow-up meeting in 1h.
Chris: After we stabilize, we should run an allocation audit for last 7 days to find spillovers. I’ll prepare a query.
Samir: Thanks team. If queue rises again, escalate to infra lead and consider emergency scale with preemptibles.
Mae: Will update if anything changes. Current last snapshot: queue=57, GPU util=62%, throttling=0.5%.
Samir: Closing initial mitigation phase. Folks, great triage. Postmortem owners: Mae (lead), Lia (infra), Chris (runtime). Support to coordinate customer comms.
Mae: Noted. Will create postmortem doc and link when available.
Support: Final customer update posted: "Issue mitigated; performance restored for most enterprise tenants. Ongoing follow-up and timeline for quota increases will be shared."
Samir: Incident marked as 'mitigated' at 1778210559. Leaving channel.
Mae: Leaving channel, continuing follow-ups in #eng-infra.
